intro: Finalist Brief: Humor Genome, Build with Gemma. Seven submissions, analyzed on implementation, demonstration, idea, and Gemma usage. Three are worth your closer review. Here's why, with evidence from their own demos.
outro: The evidence behind each pick is one tap away in the app, along with the four other submissions that were analyzed.

segments.whySurfaced: Measures real audience laughter and tests it against Gemma's predicted beats, on video, with the signal-processing code in the repo.
segments.narration: Why'd They Laugh? measures real audience laughter from a stand-up clip and lines it up against Gemma's predicted beats. On screen: the laugh timeline, then predicted versus actual. The repo's laughter detector is real signal processing, not the model.

evidence.detail: Clip stats (28 s, 3 laughs), then the laugh timeline with detected regions.
'Predicted vs. actual — the AI's theory, tested against reality' with what worked / what fell flat.
humor_genome/laughter.py: laugh-burst detection from audio; video.py: ffmpeg frame and audio extraction.

segments.whySurfaced: Six working tools on one documented Gemma pipeline; the validate / repair / critic stages appear in both the README and the demo.
segments.narration: Humor Genome Studio puts six humor tools on one Gemma pipeline. Here, the Joke Copilot runs with the Gemma model selected in Studio Controls. The repo documents validate, auto-repair, and critic stages, and the demo shows them working.

evidence.detail: Tool grid, then Joke Copilot with Studio Controls showing the selected Gemma model.
Pipeline stages Assemble / Validate / Auto-repair / Critic pass shown on screen.
README: six-stage pipeline with schema validation, backoff retries and a fallback model chain; gemma-4-31b-it selectable.

segments.whySurfaced: A single multimodal Gemma call is the whole product, and the demo shows it working end to end on a real meme.
segments.narration: Killjoy explains why a meme is funny in a single multimodal Gemma call. Watch a sample meme go in and five structured fields come out: mechanism, cultural reference, audience, and a self-aware funniness-lost score. The model IDs are explicit in the repo.

evidence.detail: Sample meme selected, Gemma 'thinking' state, then the structured result.
Result card: mechanism, cultural reference (Distracted Boyfriend), likely audience, funniness lost 20%.
backend/humor_engine.py builds the single multimodal call to gemma-4-31b-it; schemas.py defines the five fields.
